title: av_extend_guts after an unshift leaves the trailing element slots holding stale SV pointers
live_proof: upstream fixed it in 9e298ab597 (9e298ab597b2c6fc0741749d7e29119e2d6cd628) (2023-07-18). That commit is an ancestor of v5.45.3-85-gdb19522155 and is NOT an ancestor of the v5.36.3 tag (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, both directions), so it never reached the 5.36 maintenance branch; the pin's tree shows the unfixed code (pin av.c:111 to_null = *arrayp - *allocp; av.c:118 newmax = key + *maxp; goto resize with no to_null correction). Host ASan at the pin: ASan: SEGV (rc=77); the same trigger, same harness and same ASan options on master: no report (rc=0, the harness reports [PASS])
fidelity: the trigger is the test upstream added with its own fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it

sysalloc-bounds.oracle: no fault: completes and the workload's own oracle passes

sysalloc-sublet.oracle: no fault: completes and the workload's own oracle passes
sysalloc-sublet.verdict_note: the defect is not shown reached on this arm: the trigger has no reach observation. Its only check is pass('unshifting and growing an array initializes trailing elements') (trigger.pl:13), and the harness's pass is unconditional (harness/shim.pl:8: sub pass { $CUR++; 1 }), so the run's silence says nothing about whether a stale element slot existed. RETRACTED 2026-10-11: the basis recorded on 2026-10-10 -- 'the case's own assertion passes, so the stale element slot never holds a stale pointer' -- rests on that unconditional pass and cannot support it. The NO-READING stands for the reason above.

status: all three Capstone arms measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM, each after passing its own two controls; cheribsd-revocation measured 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap, revocation selected per process because the system-wide default kills the guest's sshd, and every case run under both settings so the pair controls the knob (results/20261006-cheribsd)
allocator_layer: system allocator (the AV element array, via Renew)
note: not triggered by this trigger anywhere but the host: its own assertion PASSES on all four Capstone arms AND on CheriBSD with revocation both off and on, so the stale element slot the defect depends on never holds a stale pointer there. Its silence is not evidence about any arm and it is outside every denominator. Host ASan at the pin reports SEGV, so the defect is real; what is missing is a trigger that reproduces it under an allocator other than glibc CORRECTION 2026-10-11: 'its own assertion PASSES ... so the stale element slot the defect depends on never holds a stale pointer there' does not follow -- that assertion is pass(), which is unconditional (harness/shim.pl:8), so the trigger observes nothing about the slot. The runs show only that no arm reported the defect; whether the trigger reaches it off glibc is unknown.
fault_sites_why: Host ASan at the pin (results/20261006-host-differential, the run of 2026-10-06 before any virtual run): SEGV, frames #0-#1 Perl_SvREFCNT_dec | Perl_av_clear (sites.tsv; the interpreter's dispatch loops Perl_runops_standard and Perl_yyparse are not sites).
